title: 7 Best ServiceNow Alternatives in 2026 (and What Each One Owns)
summary: ServiceNow has no public list prices, and Gartner says its implementations take real transformation work. Seven alternatives compared on price, depth and what each one owns, all checked November 2026.
body_markdown:
*ServiceNow runs service desks at enterprise scale and prices like it. The seven alternatives below are compared on what each one owns once it's live: the service desk, the assets, the approvals and the workflows that stay with your team.*


Contents:


- Why teams switch away from ServiceNow
- Freshservice: the fast mid-market service desk
- Jira Service Management: the fit for Atlassian shops
- BMC Helix ITSM: the enterprise-depth rival
- ManageEngine ServiceDesk Plus: the budget pick
- TOPdesk: employee services beyond IT
- SolarWinds Service Desk: the middle ground
- HaloITSM: one platform for every service team
- How to choose between them
- FAQ


ServiceNow is the default when a company outgrows its first help desk. Subscription revenue grew 21% year over year to $3.99 billion in Q3 2026 \[1\], the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for IT service management, the first edition since 2022 \[3\], still names it a Leader \[2\], and the category around it keeps growing. It is also the most expensive tool to buy and the heaviest to run: no public list prices, a median contract of $129,871 a year in Vendr's purchase data \[4\], and, in Gartner's words about its implementations, a platform that "requires significant transformation and expertise" \[5\]. That combination sends a steady stream of mid-market and enterprise teams looking around.


If you want a like-for-like service desk without an implementation project, start with Freshservice. If your engineering and ops teams already work in Atlassian, Jira Service Management is the natural fit. ManageEngine ServiceDesk Plus and SolarWinds Service Desk cover the low end of the budget, BMC Helix competes at enterprise depth, TOPdesk owns employee services in Europe, and HaloITSM puts every service team on one platform at a single price. Each section below states what the tool owns and where it asks you to compromise.


## Why teams switch away from ServiceNow


Money comes first. ServiceNow publishes no list prices: its ITSM pricing page lists three packages (ITSM Foundation, ITSM Advanced and ITSM Prime) and every one of them ends in a "Get Custom Quote" button. Licensing counts fulfiller users, the people who work tickets, so the bill grows with your support headcount. Vendr, a marketplace that records real software purchases, puts the median annual contract at $129,871 across 111 recorded purchases \[4\]. I'd read that as an order of magnitude; it's a sample of 111 deals and every estate prices differently.


Time comes second. Gartner's Market Guide for ServiceNow Consulting, Implementation and Managed Services, published in April 2025, states that implementation of the platform "requires significant transformation and expertise", and that a poor implementation is the leading trigger for post-implementation services \[5\]. A Gartner Peer Insights reviewer gave the operational version of the same point in a March 2026 review: "Customizations are difficult and expensive. You will need dedicated administrators to run this platform at scale." \[6\] It's one review, though it matches what the market guide describes.


The third reason is coverage. ServiceNow sells one platform that covers IT operations, security, HR and more, and a buyer who only needs the service desk still sits inside that commercial structure. The AI story is ahead of most of the category too: in Gartner's September 2025 Magic Quadrant for AI applications in IT service management, ServiceNow was the sole Leader \[7\]. So the switch decision in 2026 usually turns on price, implementation weight and how much of the platform you end up using, with AI capability close behind.


## Freshservice: the fast mid-market service desk


Freshservice is Freshworks' cloud ITSM platform, built for mid-market speed. Its pricing page lists Starter at $19, Growth at $49 and Pro at $99 per agent per month on annual billing, with Enterprise quote-only, and the Freddy AI Copilot rides on top as a $29 per agent per month add-on (all checked November 2026). A 14-day trial unlocks the full feature set, no card needed.


What it owns is the most direct like-for-like swap in this list. Incident management, the service catalog and SLA tracking arrive from the Growth tier, change and problem management from Pro, and the admin model is light enough that a small ops team runs it without a dedicated administrator. Freshworks was named a Leader in the 2026 Magic Quadrant \[2\].


The trade-off sits in depth. If your ServiceNow instance carries years of bespoke workflow logic, Freshservice will hold the standard processes and lose the bespoke ones. The AI bill also stacks: the copilot is priced on top of every seat that uses it.


## Jira Service Management: the fit for Atlassian shops


Jira Service Management's strongest argument is that your engineers already live in it. Atlassian prices it free for 3 agents, then Standard at $21.50 and Premium at $55.28 per agent per month on annual billing, with Enterprise quote-only (checked November 2026). One planning note: Atlassian flags usage-based billing starting December 3, 2026, so read the fine print before you commit.


Where it wins is the dev-to-ops handoff. An incident raised in the service queue lands on the same Jira boards your engineers already triage, asset and configuration management ships from the Standard tier, and change management with approval workflows and AI risk assessment arrives at Premium. Atlassian was also named a Leader in the 2026 Magic Quadrant \[2\].


It fits less well outside Atlassian. If your org runs on Microsoft or Google tooling instead, the integration advantage disappears, and the asset database stays simpler than what the enterprise suites in this list offer.


## BMC Helix ITSM: the enterprise-depth rival


BMC Helix is the suite closest to ServiceNow in scope. The 2026 Magic Quadrant made it a Leader for the tenth time, according to BMC's own announcement \[2\]. The product page leads with agentic AI, AI-driven incident clustering and change risk analysis, and the documentation runs deep on ITSM process configuration.


The work it owns is the complex estate: multi-team ITSM with heavy configuration, mature change management, and a CMDB with a long enterprise track record behind it.


It's also the least transparent on price: no published rates, and the trial runs through a contact form, so budgeting means a procurement cycle before you know the number. That's normal in this segment, and it's still a real cost.


## ManageEngine ServiceDesk Plus: the budget pick


ServiceDesk Plus is the price outlier here. ManageEngine's pricing page lists Standard from $13, Professional from $27 and Enterprise from $67 per technician per month on a yearly subscription, and states the prices were current as of September 2026 (I re-checked the page in November 2026). The Standard edition is free for up to five technicians, a 30-day trial covers the product, and both cloud and on-premises editions exist.


What it owns is the budget line. A ten-technician team pays a low four figures a year where suites like BMC Helix run five or six, and incident, change and asset management are all included, with the Zia AI assistant across editions.


Depth is where it gives ground: process automation and multi-team configuration trail the enterprise suites, and the Zia agents only appear at the Enterprise tier. For a few hundred employees with one IT admin, that trade usually makes sense. At a few thousand, I would say look at the suites above first.


## TOPdesk: employee services beyond IT


TOPdesk is a Dutch ITSM suite aimed at organizations of 250 to 10,000 employees, with a strong European mid-market following. Its UK pricing page runs Essential at £51, Engaged at £72 and Excellent at £101 per agent per month on annual billing (checked November 2026), and a 30-day trial needs no credit card. The suite covers IT alongside HR and facilities requests, with EU data residency.


What it owns is the employee side of operations. When the queue covers HR requests and facilities tickets alongside the laptops and password resets, one tool removes a second contract and a second integration to maintain.


The limits show up outside Europe: presence and support thin out, and the AI capabilities are distributed by plan tier.


## SolarWinds Service Desk: the middle ground


SolarWinds Service Desk sits between the budget tools and the enterprise suites. Its pricing page lists Essentials at $39, Advanced at $99 and Premier at $124 per technician per month billed annually, with one line that matters for planning: asset management is priced separately (all checked November 2026). Essentials already covers incident management, the service catalog, change management, CMDB and SLAs, Advanced adds employee service management and a virtual agent, and Premier adds AI incident summaries and a visual CMDB. A fully functional 30-day trial covers it all.


The work it owns is the middle ground itself: you pay per technician and end users are unlimited, so the bill stays predictable while the service catalog and CMDB stay real.


Check two things before you sign: the AI features only arrive at Premier, and if asset discovery matters to your comparison, pull the separate asset quote first so the totals are comparable.


## HaloITSM: one platform for every service team


Halo prices differently from everyone else in this list: one price, no tiers. Its UK pricing page lists £69 per agent per month billed annually and states that every capability ships in that one price; the US dollar figure sits behind the region selector (checked November 2026). The platform covers ITSM, enterprise service management, customer service and PSA in a single license, with Halo AI included, and there's an enterprise option with unlimited licenses and funded implementation for a fixed one million dollars per year.


What it owns is consolidation. If you run separate tools for IT, customer service and internal requests today, one platform with one per-agent price replaces the whole stack, and named and concurrent licenses cost the same.


Note two limits before you shortlist it: an onboarding package is required with purchase, at a bespoke cost, and the one-price model only pays off when you use the breadth. If you need a plain service desk, you're funding the rest anyway.


## How to choose between them


Start from the workflow you're replacing, because "ServiceNow alternative" covers three different purchases: a cheaper service desk, a lighter enterprise platform or a consolidation play.


- If the driver is the price of the desk itself, trial ManageEngine ServiceDesk Plus and SolarWinds Service Desk first. Both have self-serve trials, so you can make sure the tool handles your real ticket mix without a procurement cycle.
- If your teams already work in Atlassian, Jira Service Management removes an integration you would otherwise build and maintain.
- If you need ServiceNow-level depth at a mid-market org, Freshservice is the fastest route and BMC Helix is the deeper one.
- If half your "IT tickets" are really HR and facilities requests, TOPdesk runs them in the same queue as everything else.
- If you're consolidating several service teams onto one platform, HaloITSM's single price is built for that decision.


And if what you're replacing sits closer to internal tooling than to ITIL, the comparison changes shape entirely: our guides on[PowerApps alternatives](https://www.vybe.build/blog/best-powerapps-alternatives) and the[best AI workflow builders](https://www.vybe.build/blog/best-ai-workflow-builders-2026) cover that side of the market.


One practical note regardless of vendor: run the trial on a real week of tickets instead of the demo data. The real differences between these tools show up in change approvals and asset records, and demo datasets never exercise either one. For what the workflows look like once they leave the desk, our piece on[connecting tools into ops workflows](https://www.vybe.build/blog/connect-tools-build-workflows-vybe) and the[operations and finance workflow examples](https://www.vybe.build/blog/operations-finance-workflow-ideas-vybe-integrations) are the closest previews we have.


## FAQ


### How much does ServiceNow cost?


ServiceNow publishes no list prices; every package on its ITSM pricing page ends in a custom quote request. The best public estimate comes from Vendr's contract data, which puts the median at $129,871 per year across 111 recorded purchases \[4\]. Licensing is per fulfiller user, so the bill scales with the number of people who work tickets.


### What's the best ServiceNow alternative for a mid-market team?


For most mid-market teams, Freshservice is the most direct like-for-like switch, and Jira Service Management wins when the company already runs Atlassian. Both sit well below ServiceNow's typical contract size, and both were named Leaders in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant \[2\].


### Is Jira Service Management a good ServiceNow alternative?


It is when your engineering and ops teams already use Jira. Incident, asset and configuration management ship with the Standard plan at $21.50 per agent per month (annual billing, checked November 2026), and change management with approvals arrives at Premium. Without Atlassian in your stack, other tools on this list fit better.


### What is the easiest ITSM tool to implement?


For small and mid-market teams, ServiceDesk Plus and Freshservice are the simplest starts: both offer self-serve trials and run on standard out-of-box processes. The enterprise suites, including ServiceNow itself, assume an implementation project, and Gartner's market guide describes why that weight exists \[5\].


### Can you migrate from ServiceNow to another tool?


Yes, and plan it as a project, because the export is the easy part. Tickets, users and attachments move through each vendor's import tooling, but workflow logic built in ServiceNow usually has to be rebuilt in the target tool, and that's where the timeline goes. None of the vendors here publish migration-duration figures, so get a migration quote during procurement.

All seven of these tools own something ServiceNow also owns, at a different weight and a different price. Price the seat math against your fulfiller count and keep implementation effort in the comparison from day one.
